name: Jamaica

findings.summary: At the opening of Huawei's new Kingston offices, Prime Minister Holness credited Huawei, active in Jamaica since 2007, with a key role in the move from GSM to UMTS and with ongoing LTE deployments.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 5 inferred from the PM describing an installed base; neither source names the operator(s), network domain (RAN/core) or share, so national scale is an upper bound. Date is the statement date, not deployment dates. The $300-million office investment has no stated currency and is not recorded as a value.

findings.summary: Huawei partnered with Digicel Group to deliver a CDMA2000 1xEV-DO network across five Caribbean markets in a first stage, Jamaica among them, enabling roaming and mobile data for CDMA customers.
findings.analyst_inference: Pre-2020 finding; whether this CDMA overlay remains in service was not checked and is likely legacy. Value not disclosed. Does not establish Huawei as Digicel Jamaica's current GSM/LTE/5G vendor.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of National Security / Jamaica Constabulary Force (JamaicaEye)
findings.summary: South Korea's government funded about 210 surveillance cameras, costing US$400,000, handed over to the Ministry of National Security for integration into the JamaicaEye centralised CCTV system used by police.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: no source names the camera manufacturer, so the equipment controller is unknown; the donor (Korea) is a financier, not the controller. JamaicaEye is operated domestically. Observer reports 215 cameras, government sources 210. Tier 4 = equipment delivered, integration pending. US$400,000 is a government-stated cost, kept as announced.

findings.summary: Government awarded two restricted-tender JamaicaEye contracts worth about J$790 million: Sitewatch Electronic Security to supply and install 300 CCTV cameras in Portmore, and Konnexx Services for islandwide maintenance.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: contractors are local integrators and the article names no camera or platform vendor. Value in Jamaican dollars, not converted. Ministry declined to give deployment details.

facilities.null_reason: one search for Jamaican data-centre or AI-campus projects since 2023 found none; ministerial AI speeches named no facilities

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases or export-licence reporting surfaced in facilities/models searches; silicon not given a dedicated search

models.null_reason: two searches and two government pages (AI task force directive May 2026, Minister Vaz April 2025) named no frontier model provider partnership or national model

research_gaps: Who supplies Flow Jamaica's (Liberty Latin America) 5G RAN/core launched June 2026, and Digicel Jamaica's current LTE/5G RAN and core? Is Huawei still a supplier to either?
Which operators and network domains does the PM's 2022 credit to Huawei (UMTS, LTE) refer to?
Camera manufacturers and video-management platform behind JamaicaEye, including the Korean-funded cameras and the 2026 Sitewatch Portmore contract.
Any government adoption of a frontier model (e.g. Microsoft Copilot, OpenAI, Google) following the National AI Task Force's work and the pending National AI Policy.
Submarine cable landings in Jamaica and their system vendors (any HMN Tech involvement).
